correctness.rationale: For finite Dirichlet punctured lattice balls S_{d,R}, a signed-permutation orbit reduction gives the exact integer identity D(4E-(d-2)^2H). Independently generated orbit representatives, multiplicities and adjacency counts with JS BigInt directly from assigned certificate.json (not by running its verifier). At d=9,R=23 exactly 90 orbits and positive integer h give minimum scaled supersolution slack 100963; the discrete ground-state identity upgrades this to strict positivity on every complex-valued test, not just invariant ones, and hence all R<=23. At R=24 exactly 98 orbits give D=5354228880 and negative scaled defect -3740776448633821897328. Independently checked d=10,R=3 defect -5760 with D=6; d=11,R=2 defect -2332 with D=2; d=12,R=1 defect -96. Smaller radii are excluded by exact one/two-shell eigenvalue calculations; for all d>=12 the one-shell inequality follows from 2d<(d-2)^2/4. Published full-lattice Hardy theorems supply infinity for d<=8. This is a mathematically exact finite certificate combined with analytic ground-state/Perron-Frobenius arguments, not a finite numerical extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Lizama established failure in dimensions nine and ten globally, and Alpay established the coefficient through dimensions five to eight. Those theorems do not identify the first squared-Euclidean-radius Dirichlet ball violating the dimension-nine coefficient. A negative witness at radius 24 alone would not show minimality; the new 90-orbit positive supersolution at 23 is essential.
